title: mavai declarative contract file (mavai-contract/1)
description: Structural schema for the mavai family's declarative contract file. It validates the parsed data model of the YAML document (YAML is the file encoding; the schema addresses the resulting structure). The canonical specification is the prose format specification maintained in the family's internal requirements catalog (MAVAI-CONTRACT-FORMAT.md, v0 frozen; amendment session 2026-07-25; value-comparison amendment 2026-07-27); this schema is its machine-checkable structural projection and never introduces a rule the specification does not state — $comment fields cite the mandating sections. Semantic obligations the schema cannot express (view-reference resolution, per-input expectations requiring a single criterion, selection-expression syntax, non-decreasing latency ceilings, file-path resolution, ...) are carried by the conformance corpus manifest. These artefacts are family engineering infrastructure — schemas the implementing frameworks conform to — not a standard for third-party implementations.

format.$comment: Part I, Keys: the format identifier MUST be mavai-contract/1 for this version.

contract.$comment: Part I, Keys: author-chosen name; the instantiated contract's identity (SII.2).

service.$comment: Part I, Keys: the name of the registered service binding (SII.3).

propertyNames.$comment: Part I, Views / SII.10: raw is the reserved name of the untransformed response and cannot be declared as a view.

additionalProperties.$comment: Part I, Views: json/xml/yaml are the stock transformations; any other value names a transformation registered in code (registry resolution is semantic, manifest-carried).

criteria.$comment: Part I, criteria section: a list of one or more criterion entries, each its own Bernoulli stream with its own threshold. Criterion-name uniqueness is semantic, manifest-carried.

inputs.$comment: Part I, Keys: the fixed, finite input list — the pool the engine cycles over (SII.4). Value shapes per Part I's input-values section (amended 2026-07-25).

intent.$comment: Part I, Keys: verification (default) or smoke (SII.5).

confidence.$comment: Part I, Keys / SII.4: contract-level confidence level; default 0.95.

facets.$comment: Part III: reserved seam (shape normative, semantics reserved) — a v0 reader rejects facets: with a pointer to the extension-seams section.

covariates.$comment: Part III: reserved seam — rejected by a v0 reader with the seam pointer.

budget.$comment: Part III: reserved seam — rejected by a v0 reader with the seam pointer.

kind.$comment: Part V, run-mode amendment 2026-07-07: kind: is withdrawn — the run mode is the invocation verb.

samples.$comment: SII.4, invocation-time-sizing amendment 2026-07-08: sample sizing left the file — refused naming the --samples flag.

samples-per-config.$comment: SII.4 / Part III explore seam: withdrawn file key — refused naming the --samples-per-config flag.

scalar.$comment: Part I, input-values section / MAVAI-SERVICES-FORMAT.md SII.7: a scalar input, passed to the binding as-is.

numberOperand.$comment: Part I, value comparison (2026-07-27): a numeric form's operand — a number, or a numeric string (sign/decimal/exponent; quoted where the file encoding's number parsing could lose the intended decimal). Comparison is decimal, not binary float.

setOperand.$comment: Part I, value comparison (2026-07-27): a set form's operand — at least one element; elements compared by strict JSON value (numbers numeric/decimal, strings exact, booleans and null by identity).

text.$comment: Part I, input-values section (amended 2026-07-25): inline text, or {file: <path>} decoded as UTF-8 text.

file.$comment: Part I, input-values section: the kind with no model wire form — deliver-to-binding only.

filePart.$comment: Part I, input-values section (amended 2026-07-25): a file-sourced part — a single-key mapping; the kind is named by the author, never sniffed. Path resolution (relative to the contract file, read at load time, content-hashed into the input identity) is semantic, manifest-carried.

oneOf.$comment: Part I, input-values section / MAVAI-SERVICES-FORMAT.md SII.7: a flat list of scalars, splatted positionally across the binding's parameters.

Part I, input-values section (amended 2026-07-25): parts in message order, forming one ordered multimodal message; a single-part list is the bare part. A list mixing scalars and parts is refused — the disjunction here admits no mixed list.

threshold.$comment: Part I, criteria section: required success rate in (0,1); normative by definition. threshold: empirical stays reserved (Part III) — the string fails this type, as mandated.

tolerate.$comment: Part I / Part V risk-claim amendment 2026-07-12: the empirical criterion's risk claim — the worst true rate the operator accepts, an absolute rate in (0,1).

confidence.$comment: Part V risk-claim amendment 2026-07-12: a per-criterion confidence on an empirical criterion, overriding the contract default.

threshold-origin.$comment: Part III, threshold provenance: sla / slo / policy — a closed set, an unknown origin is refused (clarified 2026-07-25).

is-null.$comment: Part I, value comparison (2026-07-27): is-null takes the literal true as its only operand — the negation is not offered.

is.$comment: Part I, boolean comparison (2026-07-27): boolean identity — the operand is strictly a boolean; the subject must be JSON true/false itself, never its string or numeric projection.

not.$comment: Part I, criteria section: tolerate: alongside threshold: is refused — a stipulated bar has no baseline claim to protect.

confidence.$comment: Part I, criteria section (clarified 2026-07-25): a per-criterion confidence: is the empirical criterion's alone — beside threshold: it is refused.

criterion.$comment: Part I, criteria section: content is one or more postcondition forms — declared directly (a compatible subset, all holding together) and/or as a postconditions: list; every criterion declares at least one form of its own (confirmed 2026-07-25). Direct forms judge raw; in:/path: qualifiers belong on postcondition entries.

in.$comment: Part I, subject rule: every form judges the view named by its in: qualifier; omitting in: means in: raw. That the named view is declared is semantic, manifest-carried.

path.$comment: Part I, subject rule / SII.10: a selection expression (JSONPath RFC 9535 or XPath 1.0) addressing the subject view's structured value. Expression parseability is semantic, manifest-carried.

parses.$comment: Part I, forms catalogue: parses: <view> — the named transformation succeeds on this response. That the view is declared is semantic, manifest-carried.

is-null.$comment: Part I, value comparison (2026-07-27): is-null takes the literal true as its only operand — the negation is not offered.

is.$comment: Part I, boolean comparison (2026-07-27): boolean identity — the operand is strictly a boolean; the subject must be JSON true/false itself, never its string or numeric projection.

count-equals.$comment: Part I, value comparison (2026-07-27): the selection's cardinality — count-equals: 0 holds on an empty selection.

path.$comment: Part I, subject rule / value comparison (2026-07-27): path requires an in: naming a declared view (the raw response is unstructured text), and only a string or value-comparison form MAY carry path:.

parses.$comment: Part I, subject rule (clarified 2026-07-25): parses: judges the response itself and names the view under test as its argument — it takes no in: qualifier.

postconditionEntry.$comment: One postcondition entry: exactly one form, optionally in:-qualified, string and value-comparison forms optionally path:-qualified under a declared view; set forms require both (value comparison, 2026-07-27).

setFormAddressing.$comment: Part I, value comparison (2026-07-27): a set form judges the selected values collectively and REQUIRES an in: naming a declared view and a path: — there is no collection over the raw text or a scalar.

expectedEntry.$comment: Part I, input-specific postconditions (clarified 2026-07-25): the full form vocabulary except parses: — parseability is a property of the response under a view, not of one input; declare it once as a criterion-level form.

expected.$comment: Part I, input-specific postconditions: a single form (sugar) or a list of postcondition entries. Legal only with exactly one criteria entry — semantic, manifest-carried.

oneOf.$comment: Part I, input-specific postconditions: an {input, expected} entry carrying input-specific expectations.

confidence.$comment: Part III, latency seam (clarified 2026-07-25): legal on either shape — the derivation confidence for empirical bounds, recorded provenance for explicit ceilings.

latency.$comment: Part III, latency (amendment 2026-07-09): two mutually exclusive shapes — explicit per-percentile millisecond ceilings (positive integers; the non-decreasing constraint is semantic, manifest-carried) or empirical: percentiles with baseline-derived bounds. Judged on test runs only.
